options: Merges two threads into one core
quiz.explain: `.join()` blocks the current thread until the spawned thread completes. Without it, main might end and cut the worker off mid-task.

quiz.q: Why do you often need `move` in `thread::spawn(move || { ... })`?
options: It makes the thread run faster
It gives the thread ownership of the values it uses, so they can't be dropped out from under it
It moves the thread to another CPU core
quiz.explain: `move` transfers ownership of captured values into the thread. Otherwise the compiler can't prove the borrowed data outlives the thread.

quiz.q: You need several threads to co-own and mutate one counter safely. What do you reach for?
quiz.explain: `Arc` provides thread-safe shared ownership and `Mutex` provides one-at-a-time mutation. `Rc`/`RefCell` are single-threaded and won't compile across threads.

quiz.q: What do the standard channel functions in `std::sync::mpsc` give you?
options: A pipe: a sender (tx) and receiver (rx) for passing messages between threads
A way to disable the borrow checker
quiz.explain: `mpsc::channel()` returns a (tx, rx) pair. Threads communicate by sending messages down the pipe rather than sharing memory directly — the safest sharing style.

flashcards.front: Start work on a new thread?
flashcards.back: `thread::spawn(|| { ... })` returns a JoinHandle; call `.join()` to wait for it.
`Rc` is shared ownership for a single thread (faster); `Arc` is the thread-safe version for sharing across threads.

flashcards.front: Safest way for threads to communicate?
flashcards.back: Channels (`std::sync::mpsc`) — send messages through a tx/rx pipe instead of sharing mutable memory.
`Send` = safe to move to another thread; `Sync` = safe to share by reference across threads. The compiler checks them automatically.
